children.name: The AI Enablement Audit
children.blurb: An AI enablement audit is a structured review of how an organization adopts, operates, and governs artificial intelligence.

children.name: Threat Modelling for Legal AI
children.blurb: Threat modelling for legal AI identifies ways a legal AI system can fail, be misused, or be attacked, and maps those failures to harm for clients, lawyers, and courts.

children.name: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
children.blurb: This page covers data loss prevention and sanitisation for artificial intelligence systems in enterprise settings.

children.name: Shadow AI in Legal Teams
children.blurb: Shadow AI in legal teams is the use of generative AI and other machine learning tools by lawyers, paralegals, and support staff without the knowledge or approval of the firm's IT, security, or compliance functions.

children.name: Bias Testing and Alignment
children.blurb: Bias testing and alignment in enterprise AI audits covers two related checks.

sections.body: This field is about checking how legal teams actually use AI and making that use safe enough for a firm. It includes audits that look at what tools are switched on, threat modelling that maps how a legal model could be attacked or misled, data loss prevention that stops client material leaking into training or logs, shadow AI that finds unapproved tools, and bias testing that checks outputs against protected characteristics. The work is practical, not theoretical, and it is happening now inside law firms and legal operations teams.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Enablement audits are common but often shallow, checking for tool names rather than how prompts and documents flow. Threat modelling for legal models is still early, because most firms do not control the underlying model and cannot see its training data. Data loss prevention is partly solved for email and document stores, but sanitisation of prompts and retrieval contexts remains hard. Shadow AI is widespread and hard to measure, and the site's count of 732 AI tools shows how many options a legal team could adopt without review. The honest limit is that no audit can guarantee a model will not leak or discriminate in a new case.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The AI Enablement Audit is the entry point, showing what a firm has deployed and where the gaps are. Threat Modelling for Legal AI takes that inventory and asks what could go wrong if an opponent or a bad input targets the model. Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation covers the controls that stop client data from leaving the firm or entering a training set. Shadow AI in Legal Teams looks for the tools that the audit missed because staff adopted them without approval. Bias Testing and Alignment closes the loop by checking whether the model's outputs stay within the firm's professional obligations. A reader would start with the audit, then move to threat modelling for risk, to data loss prevention for controls, to shadow AI for blind spots, and to bias testing for output quality.
